    Reaction-diffusion spread model specification

    Source: R/parsnip-models.R
    inv_reaction_diffusion.Rd

    inv_reaction_diffusion() defines Skellam's (1951) model of an invasion spreading from a point release by diffusion (coefficient D) and exponential growth (rate r). Density at distance x and time t is N0 / (4 * pi * D * t) * exp(r * t - x^2 / (4 * D * t)), so the radius at which density falls to the detection threshold c is

    Usage

    inv_reaction_diffusion(
  mode = "regression",
  engine = "skellam",
  growth_rate = NULL,
  diffusion = NULL
)

    Arguments

    mode

    Must be "regression".

    engine

    Only "skellam".

    growth_rate

    Optional fixed intrinsic growth rate r. Estimated when NULL.

    diffusion

    Optional fixed diffusion coefficient D. Estimated when NULL.

    Value

    A model specification of class inv_reaction_diffusion.

    Details

    R(t) = sqrt(4 * D * t * (r * t + log(K) - log(4 * pi * D * t))),

    where K = N0 / c. D, r and K are estimated by least squares from observed range radii, and the radius tends to the Fisher-Skellam asymptotic speed 2 * sqrt(r * D). The single predictor must be the time since introduction (positive) and the outcome the range radius, for example the output of inv_spread_rate().

    References

    Skellam, J. G. (1951). Random dispersal in theoretical populations. Biometrika, 38, 196-218. doi:10.1093/biomet/38.1-2.196

    Examples

    radius <- data.frame(years = 1:30)
radius$radius_km <- sqrt(4 * 50 * radius$years *
  (0.5 * radius$years + log(1e4) - log(4 * pi * 50 * radius$years)))
spec <- inv_reaction_diffusion() |> parsnip::set_engine("skellam")
fit <- parsnip::fit(spec, radius_km ~ years, data = radius)
fit
#> parsnip model object
#> 
#> <inv_rd_fit> Skellam reaction-diffusion model
#> Diffusion D = 50, growth rate r = 0.5, log K = 9.21
#> Asymptotic speed 2 * sqrt(r * D) = 10 distance units per time unit
predict(fit, data.frame(years = c(40, 50)))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 1
#>   .pred
#>   <dbl>
#> 1  391.
#> 2  488.
